newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA SETS UP EXCHANGE FOR SMALL MINING FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA SETS UP EXCHANGE FOR SMALL MINING FIRMS.

text.p: A Southern African Developing Mining and Mineral Industry Exchange (DEMINDEX) has been established to represent small- and medium-scale mining operators outside the major mining houses.

Announcing the formation of DEMINDEX, former mineral and energy affairs minister Pik Botha referred to it as "a bold new strategy to mobilize South Africa's multi-billion rand developing mining industry".
"There is perhaps more potential for short-term job-creation in the developing mining industry (DMI) than perhaps anywhere else," he said.
DEMINDEX said the DMI could be a major driving force behind black empowerment, with some estimates predicting 40,000 to 50,000 jobs could be created.

"The DMI is already a substantial contributor to the economies of Southern African countries, gold mines alone producing more than 40 tonnes a year -- worth about $500 million. This takes no account of mining of other key minerals, precious and semi-precious stones," the organisation said.
DEMINDEX also announced that it planned to launch an annual minerals exchange in Durban next October, which would be the one of the first trading floors of its kind in the southern hemisphere.
Botha said that in its search for black involvement, DEMINDEX was negotiating co-operation agreements with black mining organisations representing small-scale miners.
He added that one of DEMINDEX's chief objectives would be to provide access to prosperity through education, technical, financial, legal and commercial support.
DEMINDEX said it was currently canvassing local and international financial and institutional support.
